_doc: Namek's people (docs/LIVING_WORLD.md 4f, v0.166.0): lines merged into the core nodes (extend_say). Namekians live on water alone, tend Ajisa trees, keep to their elders and revere the Grand Elder; their villages are small and far apart.

text: Greetings, traveler.
Ah, a visitor. Be welcome.
The suns are kind today, are they not?
You are not of Namek, I think. I am {npc}. Be welcome in our village.
An outsider! It has been long since one came. I am {npc}.
Welcome. I am {npc}, elder of this village. Speak, and I will listen.
I am {npc}. I have kept this village for many years. What brings you so far?
Mind the young Ajisa, they are tender. I am {npc}. I tend the groves.
Hello! {npc}. The trees and I were just talking. Well, I was.
Stop there. I am {npc}, and I watch over this village. Your ki is strong. Use it kindly.
I am {npc} of the warrior clan. Come in peace and you will find peace.
Are you a fighter? I am {npc}! One day I will be a warrior like the ones in the old stories.
Hi! I'm {npc}. Do Earthlings really eat food? All of it?
{npc}. I was born here, as were my elder's children. We live quietly.
I am {npc} of the dragon clan. I grow things and I keep the water clean.
I am {npc}, the elder. Every village has one. We guide, we remember, and we keep what must be kept.
An elder listens more than he speaks. I am {npc}; ask, and I will tell you what I know.
{npc}, of the warrior clan. Few of us are left. We guard the villages and the Grand Elder.
I fight so the others need not. That is the way of my clan.
The Ajisa groves are {where:field} from here. They give us shade, and the land gives us water.
I tend the Ajisa. They took the land back after the great storm, and we help them.
My place is in the elder's house, {where:plaza} from here. The villagers come to me with their troubles.
I keep the village. Its people, its water, its memory.
Work? I carry water from the spring and keep my house. Namekians need little.
We have no shops here. We share what we have, and we need only water.
{town} is small, as our villages are: a few houses, the elder's house, the spring and the groves.
There are few of us, and the villages are far apart. The Grand Elder watches over us all.
Open land on every side. Nothing comes near without my seeing it.
Strangers come to Namek more often now. I want this village to be ready.
The Grand Elder grows old. I think of what will come after.
If the rains are good, the young Ajisa will take root before the next generation.
A grove takes a lifetime to grow. It is good work.
Water, sunlight, quiet. What more could anyone want?
The three suns never set here. One learns to rest anyway.
The spring runs clear today.
Have you heard? A ship landed beyond the far islands.
The Ajisa are flowering early this year.
The Grand Elder's house can be seen from the hills, on a clear day.
